- Model consistently underestimates prices in the early part of the forecast horizon, especially for the first 5–10 days.
- Model overestimates prices after sharp spikes (e.g., post-79.80 or 80.24), showing persistent overshoot.
- Model fails to capture mean reversion toward lower levels after peaks; tends to hold high forecasts longer than observed.
- Forecast bias is more pronounced in the second half of the 30-day window, with model overestimating mid-to-late period prices.
- Model exhibits lag in responding to recent price drops; often takes 2–3 days to adjust downward.
- Model underestimates the magnitude of price declines during sharp corrections (e.g., 80.24 → 63.10).
- Model overestimates volatility in the early days, especially when prices are trending upward.
- Model tends to smooth out short-term volatility, underestimating sudden drops or spikes in the true outcome.
- Model often fails to account for seasonal or calendar-driven price patterns (e.g., end-of-month corrections).
- Model overfits to recent high prices, leading to persistent overestimation in the 10–20 day window.
